title: rcf audit test-strength: symbol-level Python Code Nodes judged through the host python3, and the Python def anchor
summary: Test strength judges Python sources: a symbol-level .py Code Node (a def, a class, or Class.method) is read through the host's python3 with the standard library ast module only and mutated with the JavaScript operator set (stubToThrow, noOp, callRemoval), so a Python product's strength record judges each criterion instead of blocking every one, in the TestStrengthReport v1 shape unchanged; python3 absent or below 3.9 is a per-criterion BLOCKED naming python3 and the floor; a Code Node #symbol on a Python def resolves at rcf define validate. AC-19901-10 succeeds the retired AC-19901-9 with the 0.42.0 readable set.
approach: One write hand at a time, in the order of the criteria. 1 The probe and the structure reader: python3 resolved from PATH once per run and its version read (python3 --version); absent or below 3.9 is a per-criterion BLOCKED detail, never a throw; one short constant Python program over stdin and stdout, standard library ast only, returns each top-level def and class with its methods (name, async, decorators, the constructor flag) and each body's span, and the statement-level call sites of a named function or method. Splicing stays in JavaScript, so the rest of each file is byte-identical, and every mutant is written to the audit's working copy only. 2 The mutants: stubToThrow raises at the body's own indentation, noOp is pass, callRemoval turns each statement-level call into None across the project's .py files only (notApplicable where there is none); a class's targets are its methods other than __init__; Class.method names one; the kill rule is the JavaScript one. 3 The per-criterion view loop routes .py Code Node files to the reader; JavaScript and TypeScript criteria in the same scope are judged as before; a .py bound test file and a file-level .py Code Node keep today's handling (BLOCKED, and the whole-run exit 2). 4 Python symbols skip the silent-default scan (silent-default parity for Python is not in this spec). 5 One def anchor in the Code Node resolver, text-level like the others. The fixture project test/fixtures/py-strength/ (no npm dependencies, no keychain, no network, no secrets) is the in-repo proof.
